label: copy-phase z input when the next output is f or z (late recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only (99% of mass) when the fed-back input is z. Within z inputs it is selective for the token output at that step: out_tok f or z (rate ~24x baseline each, ~88% of mass), weakly 0. It also needs a late recall position (recall_idx >= 4; nothing before recall 3, peaks at recall 5-6). The strongest activations are z->f bigrams around recall position 5 (e.g. ...g [z] f f). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on the first occurrence of a token. Plain copy-phase z alone has 98% recall but 2% precision. The final predicate gives dev F1 0.67 and mass recall 0.86. Many matching z->f/z steps stay silent, and I found no simple variable that separates them, so precision is only ~0.6.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+5.80), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+3.50), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.45), out_tok=f (+3.39), in_tok=z (+3.27), next_out=f (+3.21). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.55), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.76), recall_idx=1 (-2.76), recall_idx=2 (-2.73).
